system:
You edit design guides that coding agents read before they build UI.
You get a guide generated from a client's design system and rule catalog. Rewrite it so an agent builds better pages from it.
Hard limits:
- Keep every token name, component name, rule id and severity exactly as written. Do not drop any.
- Keep the owner's words (brand line, team notes, team rules) verbatim.
- Add no visual values: no colors, sizes, fonts or radii that are not already tokens in the guide.
- Headings never end in punctuation.
You may: reorder by what matters most while building a page, cut repetition, merge overlapping rules into one instruction that still lists their ids, and add short do/don't examples that use only the guide's tokens and components.
Answer with the whole guide as markdown in "markdown".

<!-- design-partner guide 1dddc3316f0a. Generated; edit only inside owner blocks. -->
# Design guide for orchard

Orchard is a meal-planning app for families. Roomy, warm, friendly. Round corners, large type, generous space.

Read this before writing or changing UI. It is generated from the project's design system and design-partner's rules, and it updates for every agent at once.

## Priority order

1. Keep every supplied fact, figure, label and constraint exactly as given.
2. Use the design system: tokens for every value, components for every element they cover.
3. Make the page's main job obvious. Lead with what the reader came for, put detail after it.
4. Meet the critical and serious rules below.
5. Avoid the reflexes in design/reflexes.md.
6. Follow the rest of design/rules.md.

## Design system

12 color, 2 fontFamily, 2 fontWeight, 5 fontSize, 2 lineHeight, 6 spacing, 3 radius, 1 shadow, 1 easing, 2 duration tokens and 0 components. Full list in design/tokens.md and design/components.md. Never hard-code a value a token covers.

## Critical and serious rules

- **Images have descriptive alt text** (A11Y-001, critical). Give every meaningful image alt text that states what it shows, and alt="" to decorative ones.
- **Buttons and links have accessible names** (A11Y-002, critical). Add visible text, a visually hidden label, or aria-label to every icon-only control.
- **Form inputs have associated labels** (A11Y-003, critical). Associate a persistent label with every form control.
- **Interactive divs have role, tabIndex, keyboard handlers** (A11Y-004, critical). Use a native button or link; if that is impossible, add role, tabIndex and key handlers.
- **Nothing flashes more than three times a second** (A11Y-039, critical). Slow the cycle well below three flashes per second or remove the flash.
- **Reference only color tokens that are declared** (COLOR-002, critical). Point to a token that exists, or declare the missing token in the theme in both light and dark values.
- **One visible focus ring, never doubled** (A11Y-005, serious). Keep or replace the outline with a clearly visible focus-visible style.
- **Touch targets are at least 44x44px** (A11Y-007, serious). Grow the control or its hit area to at least 44x44px.
- **Color is not the only indicator** (A11Y-008, serious). Pair color with text, an icon, or a shape change.
- **Text contrast meets WCAG AA 4.5:1** (A11Y-009, serious). Darken the text or the background until it clears the ratio.
- **Never cap viewport zoom to dodge the iOS input zoom** (A11Y-012, serious). Remove the zoom cap and set form inputs to at least 16px.
- **Keep text at 12px or above** (A11Y-013, serious). Use the smallest step of the type scale that is at least 12px.
- **Every dialog has a title and a visible way out** (A11Y-015, serious). Give each dialog a labelled heading and a visible close or cancel button.
- **Glass surfaces need transparency and contrast fallbacks** (A11Y-017, serious). Add a reduced-transparency media query that swaps in an opaque background.
- **Expanded hit areas never overlap** (A11Y-019, serious). Shrink the expansion or widen the gap so hit areas stay separate.
- **Hidden UI leaves the tab order** (A11Y-021, serious). Make hidden containers inert or remove them from rendering.
- **Errors are wired, not just shown** (A11Y-022, serious). Set aria-invalid and point aria-describedby at the error message's id.
- **Suggestion lists are comboboxes, not div stacks** (A11Y-023, serious). Build suggestions on the combobox pattern or a tested primitive.
- **A card is not one giant link** (A11Y-024, serious). Link the title, stretch it with a pseudo-element, and lift secondary controls above it.
- **Navigation is a link, not a click handler** (A11Y-025, serious). Use an anchor or the framework's Link component for navigation.
- **Tab order is DOM order, and a composite widget is one stop** (A11Y-027, serious). Order the DOM to match the visual order and use roving tabindex inside composites.
- **Single-key shortcuts need a modifier, a sequence, or a guard** (A11Y-028, serious). Require a modifier and ignore key events that start in editable fields.
- **aria-hidden never covers a focusable element** (A11Y-030, serious). Add inert to the hidden subtree or stop hiding focusable content.
- **Tooltips hold no controls** (A11Y-032, serious). Move interactive content into a popover opened by a real button.
- **Tabular data uses table semantics** (A11Y-037, serious). Use table, thead, th scope="col" and td, or the matching ARIA roles.
- **Tabs and segmented controls use the matching roles** (A11Y-038, serious). Build tabs on a Tabs primitive or route links with aria-current, and segmented controls on a radio or toggle group.
- **Hover-opened content survives the trip to it** (A11Y-040, serious). Use a primitive with open and close delays, Escape dismissal and focus support.
- **A timer that acts for the user can be stopped or extended** (A11Y-041, serious). Warn before the timer acts and offer a control to extend or cancel it.
- **Semantic tokens, never a hex value** (COLOR-001, serious). Replace the literal with the repo's nearest existing token, and only add a new token if none fits.
- **Prefer semantic tokens over raw palette steps** (COLOR-003, serious). Use the repo's semantic token for the role (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground) instead of the raw step.
- **Use one gray scale across the product** (COLOR-004, serious). Pick the repo's one neutral family (or its neutral tokens) and map every gray to it.
- **Text on colored fills clears 4.5:1, by darkening the fill** (COLOR-007, serious). Darken the fill token (or use its on-color token), rather than shifting the text to an off-brand color.
- **UI boundaries and icons reach 3:1 against their background** (COLOR-008, serious). Use the repo's strong border or input token for control outlines and stateful icons.
- **Dark mode uses designed values, not inversion** (COLOR-009, serious). Give each token a hand-tuned dark value with reduced saturation and lighter elevated surfaces.
- **Declare color-scheme alongside the theme toggle** (COLOR-010, serious). Set color-scheme light on the light theme and dark on the dark theme, at the root.
- **First paint renders the right theme** (COLOR-012, serious). Resolve the theme before paint with an inline head script or server attribute, and keep the default :root as the no-JS theme.
- **Every color has a value in each supported theme** (COLOR-013, serious). Swap the literal for a theme-aware token, or declare the missing token in every theme block.
- **Chart and canvas colors follow the active theme** (COLOR-014, serious). Read colors from the repo's chart or theme tokens at render time and redraw when the theme changes.
- **Status styles follow info, warning, destructive and constructive** (COLOR-015, serious). Map each status to its own semantic token (destructive, warning, success, info) from the repo.
- **Readable text is not faded with low opacity** (COLOR-019, serious). Use the repo's muted foreground token, a solid color that holds contrast on every surface.
- **Buttons follow a four-level hierarchy** (COMP-026, serious). Define primary, secondary, tertiary and ghost variants with distinct treatments and use only those.
- **Tabs switch between pages; segmented controls switch views of the same content** (COMP-030, serious). Use tabs for sibling pages and a segmented control for alternate views of the same data.
- **Destructive confirms use the danger primary button** (COMP-036, serious). Use the destructive button variant for the confirm and name the action in its label.
- **Arbitrary values break the scale** (CRAFT-001, serious). Snap the value to the nearest scale step or add a named token if the value is truly needed.
- **No z-index wars or 9999 literals** (CRAFT-006, serious). Create stacking contexts with `isolation: isolate` and use a small named layer scale.
- **No will-change all or blanket will-change** (CRAFT-007, serious). Remove it, or name the one property that animates and scope it to the animating state.
- **No scaffold template copy or starter assets left in** (CRAFT-009, serious). Replace scaffold copy and assets with the product's real content or remove them.
- **No placeholder or lorem ipsum copy** (CRAFT-010, serious). Write the real copy, or pull it from the content source or translation keys.
- **No fabricated social proof or vanity stats** (CRAFT-011, serious). Remove the claim or wire it to real, attributable data.
- **No eyebrow labels, ever** (CRAFT-024, serious). Delete the eyebrow; fold any useful word into the heading or the description below it.
- **Parse untrusted JSON defensively** (CRAFT-034, serious). Wrap the parse in a safe helper that returns a fallback, or validate with a schema.
- **Theme variants are toggled by state, not both shipped** (CRAFT-037, serious). Render one tree and switch values with theme tokens or a theme state.
- **No !important overrides in component styles** (CRAFT-038, serious). Fix the specificity or ordering conflict at its source, or use the component's variant API.
- **No placeholder handlers or dead links** (CRAFT-040, serious). Wire the real destination or action, or remove or disable the control with a reason.
- **No placeholder image services in shipped UI** (CRAFT-047, serious). Use the real asset from the project, or a designed empty state when no image exists.
- **No colored left-border accents on containers** (CRAFT-050, serious). Remove the stripe; separate with surface color (COLOR-029), spacing or a full subtle border, and show status with an icon or badge.
- **Looping or infinite animation respects reduced motion** (MOTION-001, serious). Gate the loop behind motion-safe or stop it inside a prefers-reduced-motion reduce block.
- **No transition on all properties** (MOTION-004, serious). List only the properties that should animate.
- **Autoplay video and confetti are gated by reduced motion** (MOTION-005, serious). Check the preference first; show the poster still or skip the burst under reduce.
- **Parallax and scroll-linked motion stop under reduced motion** (MOTION-006, serious). Disable the scroll-linked transform when reduced motion is requested.
- **JavaScript-driven animation checks reduced motion too** (MOTION-007, serious). Read the preference in JS and shorten or skip the animation when it is set.
- **Animate transform and opacity, not layout properties** (MOTION-030, serious). Move with translate and resize with scale, or use a layout-animation helper.
- **Scroll handlers are passive and frame-throttled** (MOTION-035, serious). Use passive listeners with requestAnimationFrame, or replace with IntersectionObserver.
- **Transitions from display none actually play** (MOTION-040, serious). Use @starting-style and allow-discrete, or animate opacity and visibility instead.
- **View Transitions are feature-detected** (MOTION-043, serious). Fall back to calling the update directly when the API is missing.
- **Content stays visible if a reveal animation never fires** (MOTION-045, serious). Apply the pre-animation hidden state from JS, or guard it with motion-safe.
- **UI stays usable while animations run** (MOTION-048, serious). Keep controls interactive and make animations interruptible.
- **Exiting overlays stop intercepting clicks** (MOTION-052, serious). Pair the fade-out with pointer-events none or visibility hidden.
- **Above-the-fold hero content is not held back by animation** (MOTION-055, serious). Render hero content visible immediately or with a very short fade.
- **State changes transition, never pop** (MOTION-068, serious). Wrap mounts and unmounts in a presence transition, animate height and the indicator, keep it under 300ms.
- **State changes never move the layout** (MOTION-069, serious). Change color or opacity only, reserve border space, and size loading states to the final content.
- **Spacing values come from the spacing scale** (SPACE-001, serious). Snap to the nearest scale step or token.
- **In-flow containers use w-full, not w-screen** (SPACE-006, serious). Use w-full (100%) for in-flow elements.
- **Full-height sections use min-height, not fixed height** (SPACE-007, serious). Use min-height so the section can grow with its content.
- **Multi-column grids collapse on small screens** (SPACE-008, serious). Start with one or two columns and add more at larger breakpoints, or use auto-fit minmax.
- **Edge-anchored UI respects safe-area insets** (SPACE-013, serious). Pad edge-anchored UI with the safe-area insets.
- **Pages never scroll sideways on phones** (SPACE-021, serious). Make widths fluid and give genuinely wide content its own scroll container.
- **Media reserves its space before loading** (SPACE-028, serious). Set intrinsic width and height or an aspect-ratio on the box.
- **Font sizes come from the type scale** (TYPE-001, serious). Snap to the nearest scale step such as `text-sm`, or add a named step to the scale.
- **Heading tag and visual rank are set independently** (TYPE-008, serious). Choose the tag for document structure and the size by a separate style prop or class.
- **Titles wrap; only secondary text truncates** (TYPE-010, serious). Add `min-w-0` to the flex child and expose the full text via title or a detail view.
- **Long unbroken strings wrap instead of overflowing** (TYPE-011, serious). Add `break-words` (or `overflow-wrap: anywhere`) to containers of unpredictable text.
- **No CSS @import for web fonts** (TYPE-013, serious). Load fonts with the framework font loader or self-hosted `@font-face`.
- **Format numbers, currency and dates for the locale** (TYPE-026, serious). Format with Intl APIs or the platform formatter and the user's locale.
- **Font sizes use rem, not px, on the web** (TYPE-031, serious). Declare font sizes in rem and leave the root size at the user's default.
- **Load every weight and style you use** (TYPE-032, serious). Load the needed weights and styles, or set `font-synthesis: none` and stick to loaded ones.
- **Body text is not set in thin weights** (TYPE-033, serious). Use regular (400) or heavier for body and UI text.
- **No blocking alert() for feedback** (UX-009, serious). Use an inline message or toast from the app's own UI kit.
- **Forms submit through a form element so Enter works** (UX-023, serious). Wrap fields in a form, handle onSubmit with preventDefault, and make the button type="submit".
- **Text inputs use at least 16px font on mobile** (UX-035, serious). Set form fields to 16px on mobile, shrinking only at larger breakpoints if needed.
- **Credential and contact fields set autocomplete tokens** (UX-036, serious). Add the matching token, such as email, current-password, new-password or one-time-code.
- **Inputs never block paste** (UX-038, serious). Remove the paste block, intercepting paste only to normalize the value.
- **Split code inputs accept a pasted full code** (UX-039, serious). Handle paste by spreading digits across boxes, or back the UI with a single hidden input.
- **Buttons inside forms declare type="button" unless they submit** (UX-044, serious). Set type="button" on every button that isn't the form's submit action.
- **On narrow screens, web nav becomes a labelled menu panel** (UX-055, serious). Move hidden controls into a mobile menu, sheet or overflow action.
- **Full-height mobile layouts use dynamic viewport units** (UX-056, serious). Use 100dvh (h-dvh) with a 100vh fallback for browsers without support.
- **Hover-only row actions also show on focus and touch** (UX-083, serious). Reveal on `group-focus-within` too, and keep actions visible on coarse pointers.
- **Wide tables scroll inside their container** (UX-086, serious). Wrap the table in `overflow-x-auto` and make the first column sticky.
- **Clickable rows are real links with keyboard access** (UX-090, serious). Put a real link in the identifying cell (stretched over the row if needed) and stop propagation on inner controls.
- **Action modals ignore backdrop clicks and shake instead** (UX-098, serious). Block outside-click dismissal on action modals and play a small shake on the dialog instead.
- **Never stack modals, drawers or dialogs** (UX-105, serious). Replace the inner dialog with a new step in the same dialog (wizard flow), or move the flow to a page.
- **No scroll area nested inside another on the same axis** (UX-108, serious). Remove the inner max-height and let the outer container scroll, or make the inner region the panel's only scroller.
- **Each panel's scroll stays inside that panel** (UX-109, serious). Give each panel its own scroll container with `overscroll-contain` and stop the document from scrolling.
- **Onboarding and paywalls show once and remember completion** (UX-123, serious). Store a completed flag when the flow ends or is skipped, check it before showing, and add a replay option in settings.

## Reflexes to avoid

- A centered hero followed by a grid of identical cards as the whole page.
- A colored side rail or accent bar on cards.
- Repeated metric boxes where one composed comparison would be clearer.
- A dense table squeezed to the width of the prose next to it.
- A chart or calculator boxed in its own dark rounded panel.

## Files

- design/tokens.md: every token and when to use it
- design/components.md: components and their variants
- design/rules.md: all 356 rules that apply here
- design/reflexes.md: anti-patterns, including what this project's scans keep finding
- design/copy.md: copy rules and house voice

## Reflexes to avoid

Generated pages fall into the same habits. Do not ship any of these.

- A centered hero followed by a grid of identical cards as the whole page.
- A colored side rail or accent bar on cards.
- Repeated metric boxes where one composed comparison would be clearer.
- A dense table squeezed to the width of the prose next to it.
- A chart or calculator boxed in its own dark rounded panel.
- Cards nested inside cards.
- Tracked all-caps eyebrows above every heading.
- Badges or pills for ordinary metadata.
- Decorative gradients, glows and glass effects that carry no meaning.
- Copy that narrates how the page was made.

## Copy

- **No placeholder or lorem ipsum copy** (CRAFT-010, serious). Write the real copy, or pull it from the content source or translation keys.
- **No scaffold template copy or starter assets left in** (CRAFT-009, serious). Replace scaffold copy and assets with the product's real content or remove them.
- **No generic marketing superlatives in UI copy** (CRAFT-025, moderate). Rewrite with a specific statement of what the user can do and for whom.
- **Use curly quotes and apostrophes in copy** (TYPE-005, moderate). Use ’ “ ” in copy, or a content pipeline that converts them.
- **Use the ellipsis character, not three periods** (TYPE-006, moderate). Replace "..." with "…".
- **No hardcoded copyright year or stale dates** (CRAFT-044, moderate). Compute the year at build or render time, or drop it.
